title: Word Formation
description: Learn word formation for Grade 6: prefixes (un-, re-, dis-, mis-), suffixes (-ness, -ful, -less, -tion), and root words — with bilingual notes, examples, practice and tests.

topics.title: Prefixes — Changing the Meaning
topics.concept:
A prefix is added to the front of a word and usually changes its meaning, often to the opposite.

PrefixMeaningExample
un-notunhappy, unkind
re-againredo, rewrite
dis-not / oppositedisagree, dishonest
mis-wronglymisplace, misuse
pre-beforepreview, prepaid
over-/under-too much / too littleovereat, underpaid

Note: a prefix usually does not change the spelling of the root — un + necessary = unnecessary (keep both n's).

examples.problem: Add a prefix to make the opposite of 'honest'.
examples.solution: dishonest — the prefix 'dis-' makes it the opposite.

recap: A prefix goes before the root and changes the meaning
un-/dis- often make opposites; re- = again; mis- = wrongly
The root spelling usually stays the same

topics.title: Suffixes & Root Words
topics.concept:
A suffix is added at the end of a word. It often changes the word's part of speech.

SuffixMakes a…Example
-nessnounkind → kindness
-mentnounmove → movement
-fuladjective (full of)care → careful
-lessadjective (without)care → careless
-tionnounact → action
-lyadverbquick → quickly

Watch the spelling: happy + ness = happiness (y → i); hope + ful = hopeful (one l).

The root word is the part left when prefixes and suffixes are removed: in unhelpfully, the root is help.

examples.problem: Add a suffix to make a noun from 'happy'.

recap: A suffix goes at the end and often changes the part of speech
The root is what remains after removing affixes

intro.en: Word formation is the art of building new words from smaller parts. A root is the base word; a prefix is added in front; a suffix is added at the end. From happy we can build unhappy (prefix) and happiness (suffix).
intro.hi: शब्द-निर्माण (Word Formation) छोटे भागों से नए शब्द बनाने की कला है। मूल शब्द (root) आधार होता है; उपसर्ग (prefix) आगे जुड़ता है; प्रत्यय (suffix) अंत में जुड़ता है। happy से हम बना सकते हैं unhappy (उपसर्ग) और happiness (प्रत्यय)।

real_life.situation:
Your teacher corrects your essay:

Teacher: You wrote carelessly. Please rewrite it more carefully — your work is untidy.
real_life.why: From one root, care, we get careless, carefully; re- means 'again' (rewrite); un- means 'not' (untidy). Knowing these parts helps you understand and spell hundreds of words.

sentence_correction.wrong: She was hopless after the loss.
sentence_correction.correct: She was hopeless after the loss.

sentence_correction.wrong: I disagreed with him strongly because he was unhonest.
sentence_correction.correct: I disagreed with him strongly because he was dishonest.

reading.passage: Sara was unhappy with her untidy room, so she decided to reorganise it. With great carefulness she sorted her books, threw away useless papers, and rearranged the shelves. Her hard work brought her real happiness, and her mother praised her thoughtfulness.

questions.q: Find two words with the prefix 'un-' or 're-'.
questions.answer: unhappy, untidy (prefix un-); reorganise, rearranged (prefix re-).

questions.q: Find a word ending in '-ness' and name its root.
questions.answer: carefulness (root: care), happiness (root: happy), thoughtfulness (root: thought).

speaking: He was unkind to the new boy.
Don't be careless with your money.

writing.prompt: Write five sentences using one word with un-, one with re-, one with -ful, one with -less, and one with -ness.
writing.example: I rewrote my untidy notes. Be careful, not careless. Her kindness was wonderful.

challenge.q: Choose the correct opposite formed by a prefix.
Identify the part of speech change: 'beauty' → 'beautiful'.
challenge.explanation: The suffix -ful turns the noun 'beauty' into the adjective 'beautiful'.

                |
   +------------+------------+
   |            |            |
 PREFIX        ROOT        SUFFIX
 un- (not)    base word   -ful/-less
 re- (again)  e.g. care   -ness/-tion
 dis-/mis-               -ly/-ment
 (front)                  (end)
revision: Prefixes change meaning: un-/dis- (not), re- (again), mis- (wrongly)
Suffixes change the part of speech: -ful, -less, -ness, -tion, -ly
Spelling: happy + ness = happiness (y→i); care + ful = careful (one l)
The root is what remains after removing affixes
